title: African flower — four colours
subtitle: A four-colour 15 cm hexagonal motif with an extended treble border
excerpt: A fourth colour adds an outer border round to the three-colour African flower, taking the motif to 15 cm and giving a second frame around the petal ring. The extra border creates a wider flat joining edge for blankets and makes the colour palette more complex without requiring any new stitches.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from the established African flower construction, extended to four-colour working. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), for multi-colour in-the-round motif conventions (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: An African flower four-colour crochet hexagon in dusty rose petals, ivory centre, olive border, and denim blue outer frame, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight. 15 cm, four colour bands clearly visible.

chartDefinition.title: African flower — four colours
chartDefinition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. A: dc centre. B: puff petals. C: inner treble border. D: outer treble border with extended corners.

glossaryTerms.definition: Several elongated half trebles drawn together at the top. Forms the petals in round 2.
Joining motifs during the final border round by replacing chain stitches with slip stitches into the matching corner of the adjacent tile.

content.text: The four-colour African flower adds one border round in a fourth colour to the three-colour version. Rounds 1 through 3 are identical; round 4 mirrors the inner border with a wider three-treble cluster group at each side and an extended ch-2 corner. The result is a 15 cm hexagon with four distinct colour bands and a flatter join edge.

Colour placement matters: the petal round (B) reads best when it contrasts both the centre (A) and the inner border (C). The outer border (D) does most of the frame work and looks good in either a neutral or a bold contrast.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 3 g Colour A, 5 g Colour B, 5 g Colour C, 6 g Colour D — all DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Each finished four-colour African flower measures 15 cm flat side to flat side (16.5 cm point to point) in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a steam-block.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
puff stitch (puff) — three elongated half trebles drawn together.
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Four colours: A (centre), B (petals), C (inner border), D (outer border). Fasten off each colour at the end of its round.
Work rounds 1, 2, and 3 exactly as the three-colour African flower (crochet-african-flower-three-colour). At the end of round 3: 6 ch-2 corner spaces, 12 ch-1 side spaces.

Join Colour D to any ch-2 corner space. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Into same corner sp work (2tr, ch 2, 3tr). Ch 1. *Work 3tr into next ch-1 side sp. Ch 1. Into next ch-2 corner sp work (3tr, ch 2, 3tr). Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * four more times. Work 3tr into last ch-1 side sp. Ch 1. Sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (72 tr, 6 ch-2 corners, 12 ch-1 side spaces.) Fasten off Colour D.

definition.title: African flower — four colours
definition.caption: Rounds 1 to 3 as three-colour version. Round 4 adds three-treble groups at each side and extended ch-2 corners.

content.text: Fasten off all ends and weave through the back of the nearest round. Steam-block pinning the six corners firmly outward to 15 cm.
on round 4, replacing the ch-2 at each joining corner with a sl st through the matched corner of the adjacent hexagon. The wider border makes the join less visible than on the three-colour version.
Handwash in cool water with mild soap, or machine-wash on a wool cycle. Lay flat to dry; do not tumble-dry.

The hexagon variant (crochet-african-flower-hexagon) changes the border construction to produce pointed hexagonal corners rather than the standard rounded corners. For a five-colour version, add a fifth round of picot edging in a contrasting colour.
